agent-skillsHow a task becomes a reviewed pull request
Overview Graph

A small set of agent skills that work like a software team. You give a task in plain words and get back a reviewed pull request that waits for your word to merge.

A skill is a file of instructions that a coding agent reads when you call it by name. These run in Claude Code and in Codex. Nothing is loaded until you ask for it.

What you type

You usually type one of two commands, followed by your task in any wording.

{{cmd:factory }}

The manager. It works out what you are asking, decides how much process the task deserves, gives the work to the right seat, has it reviewed by someone who did not write it, and brings back a pull request for you to merge.

{{cmd:improve }}

The front door only. It works out what you are asking, checks it against the project as it is today, and writes a brief: a short, clear statement of the task for the next agent. Then it stops. It writes no code.

A seat is a role on the team, like a job. You can also call a seat directly: {{typed:seats}}.

To run one step by itself, on work you already have, type {{typed:procedures}}.

The journey of one task

From your words to a pull request, in five steps.

You type {{cmd:factory}} and a task
  1. 1

    Understand

    Your words become a brief, with a size and a risk. If something is unclear, big or risky, it stops and asks you first.

    {{skill:factory}}{{skill:improve}}
  2. 2

    Hand over

    The manager gives the work to the smallest seat that can do it well. A trivial change is made on the spot, with no seat.

    {{skill:factory}}a seat
  3. 3

    Build

    The seat does the work and reports back with proof that it ran. A claim without evidence does not count as done.

    a seat{{skill:tickets}}{{skill:build}}
  4. 4

    Review

    Someone who did not write the change checks it. If they find a problem it goes back to be fixed, for a capped number of rounds.

    {{skill:review}}
  5. 5

    Ship

    The change becomes a pull request and waits at the merge gate: the checks it must pass first. The run is logged and you get a report.

    {{skill:ship}}{{skill:runlog}}
You say “merge”. Nothing is merged before that.

Who does which job

One manager, {{count:seats}} seats, a reviewer, and you. A ticket is one small piece of work that ends in one pull request.

The manager {{skill:factory}}

Decides how much process a task needs, picks the seat, checks what comes back, and reports to you in plain words.

{{skill:junior}}

Builds one ready ticket, proves it works, and opens one small pull request.

Gets: a small task.

{{skill:mid}}

Owns a feature from start to finish. Slices it into tickets, builds them or hands them to {{skill:junior}}, and reviews the pull requests that come back.

Gets: a feature of two to six tickets.

{{skill:senior}}

Owns the written plan for a project, decides when work may run in parallel, and reviews what {{skill:mid}} builds.

Gets: a project.

{{skill:10x}}

Steps in only when the team is blocked or nobody can yet say what done looks like. Frames the problem and leaves.

Gets: unclear scope, or a rescue.

The reviewer

Never the author. At least one reviewer is a model from a different provider than the one that wrote the change, because a model from the same family misses what the author missed.

The owner: you

You give the task, answer questions when the manager stops to ask, and say “merge”. No agent merges its own work.

A seat that is stuck hands the problem up: {{escalation}}
